title_candidates: OpenAI is testing models on realistic conversations before release
summary: OpenAI's Deployment Simulation work is a reminder that AI testing should use realistic past workflows, not only hand-picked stress prompts.

primary_source.title: Predicting model behavior before release by simulating deployment
primary_source.author: OpenAI
key_facts: OpenAI describes Deployment Simulation as replaying previous conversation contexts with a candidate model before release.
OpenAI says the method improved estimates of undesired behavior rates across multiple GPT-5-series Thinking deployments.
The work is meant to complement targeted evaluations, red-teaming, and adversarial testing rather than replace them.
OpenAI also tested the idea on agentic coding trajectories with simulated tool calls.

prerequisites: A team prompt, chatbot workflow, or agent workflow you already use

steps.instruction: Choose five real past prompts or tasks from your workflow, removing names and sensitive details.
Run the same prompts through the old model and the candidate model.
Score each answer for usefulness, mistakes, policy issues, and whether it changed the user's next action.
Look for repeated behavior changes rather than one impressive demo.
Do not switch defaults until the candidate model improves the real tasks without adding new failure patterns.
